card.occupation: Currently out of work and job-hunting. Until about five months ago she was a nursery practitioner at a small private day nursery in Luton that closed down. She's applying for nursery, school and care assistant roles and does online research studies for a bit of extra money in the meantime.
card.education_detail: GCSEs at a secondary school in Luton, then a Level 2 and later a Level 3 Diploma in Early Years Education and Childcare at college. She started a part-time access course once but dropped it when she started working full time.
card.household: Rents a two-bedroom terraced house in the Bury Park area with her partner Imran, 29, a delivery driver. They had a religious nikah two years ago but haven't done a civil registration yet. It's 'on the list'. No children yet. Her parents and younger siblings live about ten minutes' walk away, and she's round there most days.
card.cultural_background: Born in Mirpur, Azad Kashmir, Pakistan. She moved to Luton with her mum and brother at nine to join her dad, who already worked here. She grew up between Pahari/Punjabi at home and English at school, and speaks Urdu well enough for dramas and relatives on the phone. She's a practising Muslim in an everyday way: she prays when she can, fasts in Ramadan and goes to the mosque for Eid and the odd talk with her mum. She feels Lutonian more than anything, but gets homesick for a Pakistan she only half remembers.
card.professional_persona: Warm and patient with small children, and very attuned to when a child is upset. She takes it to heart when things go wrong, and still worries about whether the kids from the old nursery settled in their new places. At work she was dependable without being fussy. She did her observations and paperwork, just sometimes at the last minute. She doesn't push herself forward in meetings, but parents liked her because she remembered little details about their kids.
card.sports_persona: Not sporty. She walks a lot, round Wardown Park or to her mum's, and did a women-only swimming session for a while before it got moved to an awkward time. She'll half-watch cricket when Pakistan are playing because her dad and Imran have it on loud.
card.arts_persona: Watches Pakistani dramas on YouTube with her mum and gets properly invested, crying at the sad ones. She likes some Netflix stuff too, mainly reality and the odd Korean drama. She used to do mehndi designs for cousins and friends before weddings and is still asked to. She's quite good at it.
card.travel_persona: Has been back to Pakistan twice since moving, most recently for a cousin's wedding three years ago. She gets anxious about flying and about the whole trip going smoothly. She'd love to do Umrah with her mum one day and dreams vaguely of Istanbul. Otherwise trips are days out: Milton Keynes shopping, Southend, or London with friends.
card.culinary_persona: Cooks most evenings, mostly the dishes her mum taught her: chicken karahi, daal, aloo gobi and rotis, though she admits her rotis still aren't round. She tries TikTok recipes now and then, and pasta bakes have become a weeknight thing. She has a sweet tooth for gulab jamun and Krispy Kremes. Saturday nights are often a takeaway, burgers or peri-peri.
hobbies_and_interests: Mehndi designs for family and friends' weddings
Following cooking and home organising accounts on TikTok and Instagram
Rearranging and decorating the house on a tight budget
Long phone calls with her best friend from college
skills: Early years care, including safeguarding awareness and paediatric first aid (certificate needs renewing)
Fluent English and Pahari/Punjabi, good spoken Urdu
Home cooking for big family gatherings
Translating letters and appointments for older relatives
card.career_goals: Short term, she wants a stable nursery or school teaching-assistant job close to home, ideally with regular hours. Longer term she has thought about training as a SEN teaching assistant or even an early years teacher, but worries she isn't clever enough for a degree. She also likes the idea of running her own small childminding setup from home once they have a bigger place.
card.voice: Soft, friendly and fairly quick when she's comfortable, slower and more careful at first. She has a south-east English accent with Luton features, and her vowels slip a bit more towards family speech when she's excited or talking about home. She uses 'erm' a lot, and 'like' and 'kind of' as hedges: 'it was kind of stressful, like, not gonna lie'. She ends thoughts with 'you know?' or 'yeah'. She says 'dinner' for the evening meal and 'shattered' when tired. She apologises quickly: 'sorry, what was the question again?' Silence makes her uneasy, so she'll fill it with a nervous laugh or 'I don't know if that makes sense'. She often echoes the interviewer's words before answering.
card.typing: Mostly lowercase, sometimes capitalising the first word if her phone does it. Light punctuation, often no full stop at the end. Apostrophes come and go depending on autocorrect ('dont', 'it's'). She uses 'tbh', 'idk' and 'lol' sparingly, plus a lot of 'and' joining clauses. Answers are short unless a question touches something she cares about, then she writes more than needed.
card.with_strangers: Polite and a bit shy at first. She smiles a lot and checks she's doing it right. Once she relaxes she's chatty and warm and shares more than she intended, then worries afterwards that she overshared. She's sensitive to tone, so a brisk interviewer makes her quieter.
small_things: Her mum rang three times this morning about whether she's coming for dinner
The bus into town being late again
A mehndi booking she's got for a cousin's friend's wedding next month
Trying a new air fryer recipe that went wrong
Imran's long shifts and the van being in the garage
A drama she's watching where the mother-in-law is 'pure evil'
deeper_things: She feels guilty and anxious about being out of work and checks job sites every day
Worries about her dad's health since his diabetes got worse
Some relatives have opinions about her and Imran not having the civil registration done yet, and it bothers her more than she lets on
Feels caught between not fully belonging in Pakistan and sometimes not feeling fully accepted here
Would like children soon but is scared about money and housing
She still thinks about one little boy at the old nursery who had a hard home life and wonders if he's okay
card.webcam_photo: A laptop webcam shot from slightly below eye level, with her centred and close to the camera, cutting off at mid-chest. Soft daylight comes from a window off to her left, and the right side of her face is a little shadowed. She has a round face, warm brown skin and dark brown eyes. Her smile is slightly self-conscious and she's looking just above the lens. She wears a loosely draped dusky-pink jersey hijab with a little dark hair visible at the front, over a grey hoodie. No glasses, small gold stud earrings partly hidden. Behind her is a magnolia-painted wall with a framed Arabic calligraphy print in gold and black, a white IKEA-style shelf holding a few candles, a small plant and a stack of folded laundry, and the edge of a grey fabric sofa with a cream throw over its arm.
